## Quotas and budgets
- Default usage plan per team: **10,000 requests/day, 20 requests/second burst**.

## Mandatory lifecycle rules
Every bucket must have a lifecycle policy that:
1. Aborts incomplete multipart uploads after **7 days**.
2. Expires non-current object versions after **30 days** (versioned buckets).
3. For log buckets: moves objects to Glacier after **90 days** and deletes them after **400 days**, unless a legal hold applies."}, {"title": "Postmortem: Runaway Bedrock Usage (June 2026)", "section": "Lessons", "text": "Document: Postmortem: Runaway Bedrock Usage (June 2026)

Every agent loop needs a hard limit on iterations and spend. See the GenAI and Amazon Bedrock Usage Policy."}, {"title": "Lambda Error Alarm Runbook", "section": "Step 2: Common causes and fixes", "text": "Document: Lambda Error Alarm Runbook

## Step 2: Common causes and fixes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Errors spike right after a deploy | Bad release | Roll back to the previous alias/version |
| Timeouts, Duration near the limit | Slow downstream (database, external API) | Check downstream health; raise timeout only as a temporary measure |
| Throttles | Reserved concurrency too low or account limit reached | Increase reserved concurrency; check for runaway invocations |
| Errors and cost rising together | Retry storm from an event source (SQS, Kinesis) | Configure a dead-letter queue and maximum retry attempts |"}, {"title": "Cost Anomaly Response Runbook", "section": "Step 1: Identify the driver (15 minutes)", "text": "Document: Cost Anomaly Response Runbook

3. Group by the `team` and `application` tags to find the owner. If the cost is untagged, follow the Untagged Resource Remediation Runbook in parallel."}]

## Step 2: Classify the anomaly
- **Expected:** a planned launch, load test or seasonal peak (e.g. holiday promotions). Record it in #cloud-cost and close.
- **Misconfiguration:** e.g. a NAT Gateway carrying traffic that should use a VPC endpoint, debug logging left on, an autoscaling group stuck at maximum.
- **Runaway usage:** e.g. a GenAI workload calling Bedrock in a loop, a Lambda retry storm."}, {"title": "Idle Resource Cleanup Runbook", "section": "Definitions of idle", "text": "Document: Idle Resource Cleanup Runbook

## Definitions of idle

| Resource | Idle when |
|---|---|
| EC2 instance | Average CPU < 5% and network < 5 MB/day for 14 days |
| EBS volume | Unattached for more than 7 days |
| Elastic IP | Not associated with a running instance |
| Load Balancer | Zero healthy targets or < 100 requests/day for 14 days |
| RDS instance | Zero connections for 7 days |
| NAT Gateway | < 1 GB processed per day for 14 days |
| Lambda function | Zero invocations for 60 days (no direct cost, but remove for hygiene) |"}]

## Definitions of idle

| Resource | Idle when |
|---|---|
| EC2 instance | Average CPU < 5% and network < 5 MB/day for 14 days |
| EBS volume | Unattached for more than 7 days |
| Elastic IP | Not associated with a running instance |
| Load Balancer | Zero healthy targets or < 100 requests/day for 14 days |
| RDS instance | Zero connections for 7 days |
| NAT Gateway | < 1 GB processed per day for 14 days |

## Step 2: Common causes and fixes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Errors spike right after a deploy | Bad release | Roll back to the previous alias/version |
| Timeouts, Duration near the limit | Slow downstream (database, external API) | Check downstream health; raise timeout only as a temporary measure |
| Throttles | Reserved concurrency too low or account limit reached | Increase reserved concurrency; check for runaway invocations |
| Errors and cost rising together | Retry storm from an event source (SQS, Kinesis) | Configure a dead-letter queue and maximum retry attempts |"}, {"title": "Untagged Resource Remediation Runbook", "section": "S3 buckets", "text": "Document: Untagged Resource Remediation Runbook

## Mandatory lifecycle rules
Every bucket must have a lifecycle policy that:
1. Aborts incomplete multipart uploads after **7 days**.
2. Expires non-current object versions after **30 days** (versioned buckets).
3. For log buckets: moves objects to Glacier after **90 days** and deletes them after **400 days**, unless a legal hold applies."}, {"title": "Postmortem: Runaway Bedrock Usage (June 2026)", "section": "Lessons", "text": "Document: Postmortem: Runaway Bedrock Usage (June 2026)

Every agent loop needs a hard limit on iterations and spend. See the GenAI and Amazon Bedrock Usage Policy."}, {"title": "Cloud Resource Tagging Policy", "section": "Required tags", "text": "Document: Cloud Resource Tagging Policy

## Required tags
Every taggable AWS resource (EC2, EBS, S3, RDS, Lambda, EKS, Load Balancers, NAT Gateways) must carry these tags:

| Tag key | Example | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `owner` | `jane.doe@brightway.example` | A person, not a distribution list |
| `team` | `data-eng` | Must match a team in the Team Ownership Directory |
| `cost-center` | `CC-4100` | Must match the team's cost center |
| `environment` | `prod`, `staging`, `dev`, `sandbox` | Lowercase only |
| `application` | `loyalty-api` | Short application name |

Optional: `data-classification` (`public`, `internal`, `confidential`, `restricted`). Required for S3 buckets and databases."}, {"title": "S3 Storage Cost Optimization Guide", "section": "Common cost surprises", "text": "Document: S3 Storage Cost Optimization Guide

## Common cost surprises
- Versioned buckets that never expire old versions can double storage costs.
- Requests from many small objects (millions of PUT/GET requests) can cost more than the storage itself; batch small files.
- Cross-region data transfer from S3 is charged per GB. Keep compute in the same region as the bucket."}]

[{"title": "S3 Storage Cost Optimization Guide", "section": "Mandatory lifecycle rules", "text": "Document: S3 Storage Cost Optimization Guide

## Mandatory lifecycle rules
Every bucket must have a lifecycle policy that:
1. Aborts incomplete multipart uploads after **7 days**.
2. Expires non-current object versions after **30 days** (versioned buckets).
3. For log buckets: moves objects to Glacier after **90 days** and deletes them after **400 days**, unless a legal hold applies."}, {"title": "Cost Anomaly Response Runbook", "section": "Step 3: Contain", "text": "Document: Cost Anomaly Response Runbook

## Step 3: Contain
- Misconfiguration or runaway usage in non-prod: stop or scale down immediately.
- In prod: page the owning team; do not stop prod resources without the owner's agreement.
- For Bedrock or other GenAI spend, see the GenAI Usage Policy for per-team quotas and the API gateway kill switch."}, {"title": "Cost Anomaly Response Runbook", "section": "Step 2: Classify the anomaly", "text": "Document: Cost Anomaly Response Runbook

## Step 2: Classify the anomaly
- **Expected:** a planned launch, load test or seasonal peak (e.g. holiday promotions). Record it in #cloud-cost and close.
- **Misconfiguration:** e.g. a NAT Gateway carrying traffic that should use a VPC endpoint, debug logging left on, an autoscaling group stuck at maximum.
- **Runaway usage:** e.g. a GenAI workload calling Bedrock in a loop, a Lambda retry storm."}, {"title": "Idle Resource Cleanup Runbook", "section": "Definitions of idle", "text": "Document: Idle Resource Cleanup Runbook

## Definitions of idle

| Resource | Idle when |
|---|---|
| EC2 instance | Average CPU < 5% and network < 5 MB/day for 14 days |
| EBS volume | Unattached for more than 7 days |
| Elastic IP | Not associated with a running instance |
| Load Balancer | Zero healthy targets or < 100 requests/day for 14 days |
| RDS instance | Zero connections for 7 days |
| NAT Gateway | < 1 GB processed per day for 14 days |
| Lambda function | Zero invocations for 60 days (no direct cost, but remove for hygiene) |"}]

The Cost Anomaly Response Runbook (Step 2) has three: expected (a planned launch, load test or seasonal peak; record it in #cloud-cost and close), misconfiguration (for example a NAT Gateway carrying traffic that should use a VPC endpoint, debug logging left on, or an autoscaling group stuck at maximum) and runaway usage (for example a GenAI workload calling Bedrock in a loop or a Lambda retry storm).

|---|---|---|

| `environment` | `prod`, `staging`, `dev`, `sandbox` | Lowercase only |
| `application` | `loyalty-api` | Short application name |

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |

[{"title": "Cloud Cost Guardrails Policy", "section": "Thresholds and required actions", "text": "Document: Cloud Cost Guardrails Policy

## Thresholds and required actions

| Situation | Required action | Timeline |
|---|---|---|
| Spend reaches 80% of budget before day 20 of the month | Team lead reviews top 5 cost drivers and posts a summary in #cloud-cost | Within 2 business days |
| Daily spend for a service rises more than **30%** above its 7-day average | Treat as a cost anomaly; follow the Cost Anomaly Response Runbook | Same day |
| Spend exceeds 100% of budget | Freeze non-prod scale-ups; Finance and team lead approve any new resources | Immediately |
| Single new resource expected to cost > $2,000/month | Pre-approval from CCoE before launch | Before provisioning |"}, {"title": "Cloud Resource Tagging Policy", "section": "Purpose", "text": "Document: Cloud Resource Tagging Policy

## Purpose
Every cloud resource must be traceable to a team, an application and a cost center. Tags are how Brightway Retail allocates cloud spend and finds owners during incidents."}, {"title": "Cost Anomaly Response Runbook", "section": "Step 1: Identify the driver (15 minutes)", "text": "Document: Cost Anomaly Response Runbook

## Step 1: Identify the driver (15 minutes)
1. In Cost Explorer, group the last 14 days of cost by **Service**, then by **Usage type**.
2. Identify the service and usage type with the largest increase.
3. Group by the `team` and `application` tags to find the owner. If the cost is untagged, follow the Untagged Resource Remediation Runbook in parallel."}, {"title": "Postmortem: Runaway Bedrock Usage (June 2026)", "section": "Lessons", "text": "Document: Postmortem: Runaway Bedrock Usage (June 2026)

## Lessons
Every agent loop needs a hard limit on iterations and spend. See the GenAI and Amazon Bedrock Usage Policy."}]

messages.content:
[{"title": "Cloud Cost Guardrails Policy", "section": "Thresholds and required actions", "text": "Document: Cloud Cost Guardrails Policy

## Thresholds and required actions

| Situation | Required action | Timeline |
|---|---|---|
| Spend reaches 80% of budget before day 20 of the month | Team lead reviews top 5 cost drivers and posts a summary in #cloud-cost | Within 2 business days |
| Daily spend for a service rises more than **30%** above its 7-day average | Treat as a cost anomaly; follow the Cost Anomaly Response Runbook | Same day |
| Spend exceeds 100% of budget | Freeze non-prod scale-ups; Finance and team lead approve any new resources | Immediately |
| Single new resource expected to cost > $2,000/month | Pre-approval from CCoE before launch | Before provisioning |"}, {"title": "Idle Resource Cleanup Runbook", "section": "Actions", "text": "Document: Idle Resource Cleanup Runbook

## Actions
1. Confirm the owner via the `owner` tag. If untagged, use the Untagged Resource Remediation Runbook.
2. Ask the owner to confirm the resource can be removed. Allow 5 business days.
3. For EBS volumes and RDS instances, **take a snapshot before deleting**.
4. Release unused Elastic IPs immediately in non-prod accounts; they are billed even when idle."}, {"title": "Cloud Resource Tagging Policy", "section": "Required tags", "text": "Document: Cloud Resource Tagging Policy

## Required tags
Every taggable AWS resource (EC2, EBS, S3, RDS, Lambda, EKS, Load Balancers, NAT Gateways) must carry these tags:

| Tag key | Example | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `owner` | `jane.doe@brightway.example` | A person, not a distribution list |
| `team` | `data-eng` | Must match a team in the Team Ownership Directory |
| `cost-center` | `CC-4100` | Must match the team's cost center |
| `environment` | `prod`, `staging`, `dev`, `sandbox` | Lowercase only |
| `application` | `loyalty-api` | Short application name |

Optional: `data-classification` (`public`, `internal`, `confidential`, `restricted`). Required for S3 buckets and databases."}, {"title": "Cost Anomaly Response Runbook", "section": "Step 2: Classify the anomaly", "text": "Document: Cost Anomaly Response Runbook

## Step 2: Classify the anomaly
- **Expected:** a planned launch, load test or seasonal peak (e.g. holiday promotions). Record it in #cloud-cost and close.
- **Misconfiguration:** e.g. a NAT Gateway carrying traffic that should use a VPC endpoint, debug logging left on, an autoscaling group stuck at maximum.
- **Runaway usage:** e.g. a GenAI workload calling Bedrock in a loop, a Lambda retry storm."}]
Yes, if a single new resource is expected to cost more than $2,000/month. The Cloud Cost Guardrails Policy requires CCoE pre-approval before provisioning.

[{"title": "S3 Storage Cost Optimization Guide", "section": "Mandatory lifecycle rules", "text": "Document: S3 Storage Cost Optimization Guide

## Mandatory lifecycle rules
Every bucket must have a lifecycle policy that:
1. Aborts incomplete multipart uploads after **7 days**.
2. Expires non-current object versions after **30 days** (versioned buckets).
3. For log buckets: moves objects to Glacier after **90 days** and deletes them after **400 days**, unless a legal hold applies."}, {"title": "GenAI and Amazon Bedrock Usage Policy", "section": "Quotas and budgets", "text": "Document: GenAI and Amazon Bedrock Usage Policy

## Quotas and budgets
- Default usage plan per team: **10,000 requests/day, 20 requests/second burst**.
- Default GenAI budget: **$500/month per team**. Increases need ML Platform and Finance approval.
- If a team exceeds 150% of its daily average for 2 hours, the gateway throttles that key and alerts the team. ML Platform can disable a key immediately (the "kill switch")."}, {"title": "Lambda Error Alarm Runbook", "section": "Step 2: Common causes and fixes", "text": "Document: Lambda Error Alarm Runbook

## Step 2: Common causes and fixes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Errors spike right after a deploy | Bad release | Roll back to the previous alias/version |
| Timeouts, Duration near the limit | Slow downstream (database, external API) | Check downstream health; raise timeout only as a temporary measure |
| Throttles | Reserved concurrency too low or account limit reached | Increase reserved concurrency; check for runaway invocations |
| Errors and cost rising together | Retry storm from an event source (SQS, Kinesis) | Configure a dead-letter queue and maximum retry attempts |"}, {"title": "S3 Storage Cost Optimization Guide", "section": "Common cost surprises", "text": "Document: S3 Storage Cost Optimization Guide

## Common cost surprises
- Versioned buckets that never expire old versions can double storage costs.
- Requests from many small objects (millions of PUT/GET requests) can cost more than the storage itself; batch small files.
- Cross-region data transfer from S3 is charged per GB. Keep compute in the same region as the bucket."}]

[{"title": "Cloud Cost Guardrails Policy", "section": "Thresholds and required actions", "text": "Document: Cloud Cost Guardrails Policy

## Thresholds and required actions

| Situation | Required action | Timeline |
|---|---|---|
| Spend reaches 80% of budget before day 20 of the month | Team lead reviews top 5 cost drivers and posts a summary in #cloud-cost | Within 2 business days |
| Daily spend for a service rises more than **30%** above its 7-day average | Treat as a cost anomaly; follow the Cost Anomaly Response Runbook | Same day |
| Spend exceeds 100% of budget | Freeze non-prod scale-ups; Finance and team lead approve any new resources | Immediately |
| Single new resource expected to cost > $2,000/month | Pre-approval from CCoE before launch | Before provisioning |"}, {"title": "Lambda Error Alarm Runbook", "section": "Step 2: Common causes and fixes", "text": "Document: Lambda Error Alarm Runbook

## Step 2: Common causes and fixes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Errors spike right after a deploy | Bad release | Roll back to the previous alias/version |
| Timeouts, Duration near the limit | Slow downstream (database, external API) | Check downstream health; raise timeout only as a temporary measure |
| Throttles | Reserved concurrency too low or account limit reached | Increase reserved concurrency; check for runaway invocations |
| Errors and cost rising together | Retry storm from an event source (SQS, Kinesis) | Configure a dead-letter queue and maximum retry attempts |"}, {"title": "Cloud Resource Tagging Policy", "section": "Required tags", "text": "Document: Cloud Resource Tagging Policy

## Required tags
Every taggable AWS resource (EC2, EBS, S3, RDS, Lambda, EKS, Load Balancers, NAT Gateways) must carry these tags:

| Tag key | Example | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `owner` | `jane.doe@brightway.example` | A person, not a distribution list |
| `team` | `data-eng` | Must match a team in the Team Ownership Directory |
| `cost-center` | `CC-4100` | Must match the team's cost center |
| `environment` | `prod`, `staging`, `dev`, `sandbox` | Lowercase only |
| `application` | `loyalty-api` | Short application name |

Optional: `data-classification` (`public`, `internal`, `confidential`, `restricted`). Required for S3 buckets and databases."}, {"title": "Team Ownership Directory", "section": "Escalation", "text": "Document: Team Ownership Directory

## Escalation
- Cost issues: team lead, then #cloud-cost (Finance Ops).
- Security issues: #security, and page the on-call security engineer for Severity 1.
- Ownership unclear: Platform Engineering owns triage."}]

[{"title": "S3 Storage Cost Optimization Guide", "section": "Mandatory lifecycle rules", "text": "Document: S3 Storage Cost Optimization Guide

## Mandatory lifecycle rules
Every bucket must have a lifecycle policy that:
1. Aborts incomplete multipart uploads after **7 days**.
2. Expires non-current object versions after **30 days** (versioned buckets).
3. For log buckets: moves objects to Glacier after **90 days** and deletes them after **400 days**, unless a legal hold applies."}, {"title": "GenAI and Amazon Bedrock Usage Policy", "section": "Data rules", "text": "Document: GenAI and Amazon Bedrock Usage Policy

## Data rules
- No `restricted` data may be sent to any model. `confidential` data only to Bedrock (data stays in our AWS account) or the internal vLLM platform, never to external APIs.
- Prompts and responses are logged for 30 days, with customer PII masked by the gateway before logging."}, {"title": "Idle Resource Cleanup Runbook", "section": "Overview", "text": "Document: Idle Resource Cleanup Runbook

Idle resources are the most common source of avoidable spend. Run this check weekly."}, {"title": "S3 Storage Cost Optimization Guide", "section": "Common cost surprises", "text": "Document: S3 Storage Cost Optimization Guide

## Common cost surprises
- Versioned buckets that never expire old versions can double storage costs.
- Requests from many small objects (millions of PUT/GET requests) can cost more than the storage itself; batch small files.
- Cross-region data transfer from S3 is charged per GB. Keep compute in the same region as the bucket."}]
Weekly, per the Idle Resource Cleanup Runbook. It calls idle resources the most common source of avoidable spend.

- Default usage plan per team: **10,000 requests/day, 20 requests/second burst**.
- Default GenAI budget: **$500/month per team**. Increases need ML Platform and Finance approval.
- If a team exceeds 150% of its daily average for 2 hours, the gateway throttles that key and alerts the team. ML Platform can disable a key immediately (the "kill switch")."}, {"title": "Cost Anomaly Response Runbook", "section": "Overview", "text": "Document: Cost Anomaly Response Runbook

## Step 3: Cost check
A Lambda retry storm can multiply cost quickly. If invocations are more than 3x normal, follow the Cost Anomaly Response Runbook as well."}]

| Load Balancer | Zero healthy targets or < 100 requests/day for 14 days |
| RDS instance | Zero connections for 7 days |

|---|---|---|

|---|---|---|

[{"title": "Cost Anomaly Response Runbook", "section": "Step 2: Classify the anomaly", "text": "Document: Cost Anomaly Response Runbook

## Step 2: Classify the anomaly
- **Expected:** a planned launch, load test or seasonal peak (e.g. holiday promotions). Record it in #cloud-cost and close.
- **Misconfiguration:** e.g. a NAT Gateway carrying traffic that should use a VPC endpoint, debug logging left on, an autoscaling group stuck at maximum.
- **Runaway usage:** e.g. a GenAI workload calling Bedrock in a loop, a Lambda retry storm."}, {"title": "Postmortem: Runaway Bedrock Usage (June 2026)", "section": "Fix", "text": "Document: Postmortem: Runaway Bedrock Usage (June 2026)

## Fix
- Blocked direct Bedrock access in sandbox accounts with a service control policy; all calls must use the gateway.

|---|---|

Idle resources are the most common source of avoidable spend. Run this check weekly."}]

[{"title": "Cloud Cost Guardrails Policy", "section": "Thresholds and required actions", "text": "Document: Cloud Cost Guardrails Policy

## Thresholds and required actions

| Situation | Required action | Timeline |
|---|---|---|
| Spend reaches 80% of budget before day 20 of the month | Team lead reviews top 5 cost drivers and posts a summary in #cloud-cost | Within 2 business days |
| Daily spend for a service rises more than **30%** above its 7-day average | Treat as a cost anomaly; follow the Cost Anomaly Response Runbook | Same day |
| Spend exceeds 100% of budget | Freeze non-prod scale-ups; Finance and team lead approve any new resources | Immediately |
| Single new resource expected to cost > $2,000/month | Pre-approval from CCoE before launch | Before provisioning |"}, {"title": "GenAI and Amazon Bedrock Usage Policy", "section": "Data rules", "text": "Document: GenAI and Amazon Bedrock Usage Policy

## Data rules
- No `restricted` data may be sent to any model. `confidential` data only to Bedrock (data stays in our AWS account) or the internal vLLM platform, never to external APIs.
- Prompts and responses are logged for 30 days, with customer PII masked by the gateway before logging."}, {"title": "S3 Storage Cost Optimization Guide", "section": "Common cost surprises", "text": "Document: S3 Storage Cost Optimization Guide

## Common cost surprises
- Versioned buckets that never expire old versions can double storage costs.
- Requests from many small objects (millions of PUT/GET requests) can cost more than the storage itself; batch small files.
- Cross-region data transfer from S3 is charged per GB. Keep compute in the same region as the bucket."}, {"title": "Cloud Resource Tagging Policy", "section": "Purpose", "text": "Document: Cloud Resource Tagging Policy

## Purpose

## Thresholds and required actions

| Situation | Required action | Timeline |
|---|---|---|
| Spend reaches 80% of budget before day 20 of the month | Team lead reviews top 5 cost drivers and posts a summary in #cloud-cost | Within 2 business days |
| Daily spend for a service rises more than **30%** above its 7-day average | Treat as a cost anomaly; follow the Cost Anomaly Response Runbook | Same day |

## Definitions of idle

| Resource | Idle when |
|---|---|
| EC2 instance | Average CPU < 5% and network < 5 MB/day for 14 days |
| EBS volume | Unattached for more than 7 days |
| Elastic IP | Not associated with a running instance |
| Load Balancer | Zero healthy targets or < 100 requests/day for 14 days |
| RDS instance | Zero connections for 7 days |
| NAT Gateway | < 1 GB processed per day for 14 days |
| Lambda function | Zero invocations for 60 days (no direct cost, but remove for hygiene) |"}, {"title": "Postmortem: Runaway Bedrock Usage (June 2026)", "section": "Fix", "text": "Document: Postmortem: Runaway Bedrock Usage (June 2026)

## Mandatory lifecycle rules
Every bucket must have a lifecycle policy that:
1. Aborts incomplete multipart uploads after **7 days**.
2. Expires non-current object versions after **30 days** (versioned buckets).
3. For log buckets: moves objects to Glacier after **90 days** and deletes them after **400 days**, unless a legal hold applies."}, {"title": "Idle Resource Cleanup Runbook", "section": "Definitions of idle", "text": "Document: Idle Resource Cleanup Runbook

|---|---|
| EC2 instance | Average CPU < 5% and network < 5 MB/day for 14 days |
| EBS volume | Unattached for more than 7 days |
| Elastic IP | Not associated with a running instance |
| Load Balancer | Zero healthy targets or < 100 requests/day for 14 days |
| RDS instance | Zero connections for 7 days |
| NAT Gateway | < 1 GB processed per day for 14 days |
| Lambda function | Zero invocations for 60 days (no direct cost, but remove for hygiene) |"}, {"title": "Postmortem: NAT Gateway Cost Spike (March 2026)", "section": "Fix", "text": "Document: Postmortem: NAT Gateway Cost Spike (March 2026)

- Versioned buckets that never expire old versions can double storage costs.

## Mandatory lifecycle rules
Every bucket must have a lifecycle policy that:
1. Aborts incomplete multipart uploads after **7 days**.
2. Expires non-current object versions after **30 days** (versioned buckets).
3. For log buckets: moves objects to Glacier after **90 days** and deletes them after **400 days**, unless a legal hold applies."}, {"title": "GenAI and Amazon Bedrock Usage Policy", "section": "Data rules", "text": "Document: GenAI and Amazon Bedrock Usage Policy

- No `restricted` data may be sent to any model. `confidential` data only to Bedrock (data stays in our AWS account) or the internal vLLM platform, never to external APIs.
- Prompts and responses are logged for 30 days, with customer PII masked by the gateway before logging."}, {"title": "Cost Anomaly Response Runbook", "section": "Step 2: Classify the anomaly", "text": "Document: Cost Anomaly Response Runbook

## Step 2: Classify the anomaly
- **Expected:** a planned launch, load test or seasonal peak (e.g. holiday promotions). Record it in #cloud-cost and close.
- **Misconfiguration:** e.g. a NAT Gateway carrying traffic that should use a VPC endpoint, debug logging left on, an autoscaling group stuck at maximum.
- **Runaway usage:** e.g. a GenAI workload calling Bedrock in a loop, a Lambda retry storm."}]
